$comment: Shared, language-neutral block trees for the Blade-vs-JS markup parity check (#704). Consumed by both packages/visual-editor-renderer-blade/tests/Feature/RendererMarkupParityTest.php (PHP) and packages/renderer-markup-parity/tests/blade-parity.test.ts (JS). Adding a fixture here automatically exercises it against all three renderers. See README.md for the golden-file workflow.

knownDivergences.reason: Element ids differ by design. Blade mints `ap-modal-nav-N` (container) and `ap-modal-nav-N-content` from NavigationOverlayTracker so its inline script can find the drawer; React's container id comes from `useId()` (SSR-safe, `:R…:`); Vue sets none (the `^3.3` peer has no `useId`). The id values can never match, so `id` is dropped inside navigation overlay fixtures only.

RN-5: the open button's `aria-controls` points at the renderer's own container id (Blade tracker id, React `useId()`); Vue omits it because it has no SSR-stable id. The value is renderer-specific by construction. `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup` and `aria-label` are still compared.

Blade-only `data-ap-nav-overlay-open` / `-close` / `-backdrop` hooks wire the delegated inline toggle script; React and Vue bind the same behavior with component event handlers, so they have no hook attributes.

Blade emits the overlay fix-up CSS and the toggle controller once per response as attribute-less inline `<style>` and `<script>` after the first overlay nav. React and Vue need no script (component state) and ship their CSS in `<style data-ve-navigation-overlay>` (declared separately).

React/Vue inject `NAVIGATION_OVERLAY_CSS` (block-library overlay subset + the Blade fix-ups, in `@layer ve-navigation`) because JS hosts are not required to load the block-library stylesheet; Blade relies on its bundled style.css plus the inline fix-ups. The bodies differ by design, so the tag is dropped rather than compared as per-instance CSS.

Blade reads the modern flex-layout `layout.orientation` (falling back to the legacy top-level `orientation`); React/Vue read only `orientation` and default to `is-horizontal`, so a `layout.orientation: vertical` nav renders `is-vertical` only in Blade.
Blade honors `layout.justifyContent` (Keystone #52, winning over legacy `itemsJustification`); React/Vue read only `itemsJustification`, so `items-justified-*` from the modern path is Blade-only.

Nav-level `customTextColor` / `customBackgroundColor` (Keystone #53) are rendered — sanitized through `safeCssValue` — only by Blade; React/Vue do not render them at all, so `has-text-color` / `has-background` on the `<nav>` are Blade-only.
The inline `color` / `background-color` declarations those nav-level custom colors produce on the `<nav>` are Blade-only for the same reason; the only `style` attribute in this fixture is the nav's.

`ElementsSupport` (Elements API link color, `style.elements.link.color.text`) is compiled only by the Blade partial into a per-block `wp-elements-{hash}` scope class; the JS renderers have no ElementsSupport.

The scoped `.wp-elements-{hash} a:where(:not(.wp-element-button)) { color: … }` rules ElementsSupport pushes into the shared `<style data-ve-elements>` block (#852) — Blade-only, like its scope class.

fixtures.$comment: #711 — a group with the Flex Layout panel enabled at the base breakpoint and no stored `layout`. All three renderers must flip the layout class to `is-layout-flex` so the `is-layout-flow > * + * { margin-block-start: gap }` baseline rule stops pushing flex children apart.
fixtures.name: group-flex-panel

fixtures.$comment: #711 — the same panel active only from `md` up. `md:ap-flex` means 'flex starts at md', so the base-breakpoint layout class must stay `is-layout-flow` in every renderer.
fixtures.name: group-flex-panel-breakpoint-only

fixtures.$comment: #711 — an explicit `layout.type` wins over the flex panel, matching group.blade.php's `'' === $layoutType` guard.
fixtures.name: group-flex-panel-explicit-layout

fixtures.$comment: #714 — Photo Grid now emits the same `has-photo-grid` + hashed `photo-grid-<sha1>` wrapper through all three renderers (the Blade-only divergence was removed once the React/Vue ports landed). The scope hash is pinned by the golden, so a drift in either renderer's sha1/declaration surfaces here.
fixtures.name: group-photo-grid

fixtures.$comment: #714 — the same Photo Grid wrapper on a `core/columns` block. `objectFit: contain` and no `aspectRatio` exercise a different declaration string (and therefore a different scope hash) than the group fixture.
fixtures.name: columns-photo-grid

fixtures.$comment: #714 — the Photo Grid wrapper on an `artisanpack/grid` block, proving the third panel-bearing block agrees across renderers.
fixtures.name: grid-photo-grid
column-layout-constrained
fixtures.$comment: F-3 — a column carries the layout pair (flow by default) and, with a constrained content size and its own Block spacing, a `wp-container-*` scope.

fixtures.name: columns-responsive-width
fixtures.$comment: #712 — a column with the legacy scalar `width` promoted to the `base` slot plus a `responsive.width` per-breakpoint override. Exercises the merged-map hash and the `ve-w-<hash>` scope token now shared by all three renderers.

fixtures.name: columns-hostile-width
fixtures.$comment: #720 — a column whose only width is a hostile value that would close the rule and inject CSS. All three renderers must drop it: the `ve-w-<hash>` scope class is never attached, so the wrapper markup is identical across renderers (the style block itself is excluded from this markup-only check).

fixtures.name: buttons-layout-vertical
fixtures.$comment: F-3 — vertical, non-wrapping, aligned buttons with their own Block spacing get a `wp-container-*` scope plus the `is-vertical` / `is-nowrap` modifiers.
Out-of-range `columns` must clamp to the [1, 12] bounds the stylesheet has `columns-N` rules for. Blade emitted `columns-20` unclamped until 1.6.0.
fixtures.name: post-template-columns-out-of-range

fixtures.$comment: Same, at the bottom of the range.
fixtures.name: post-template-columns-zero

fixtures.$comment: Gutenberg's generic block-supports layout system stores the type on a sibling `layoutType` attribute. QueryInliner::postTemplateLayoutIsGrid() accepts it, so every renderer must lay the wrapper out as a grid too.
fixtures.name: post-template-layout-type-grid

fixtures.$comment: An upstream `core/post-template` mirror saves the object form. Third of the three shapes QueryInliner::postTemplateLayoutIsGrid() accepts.
fixtures.name: post-template-layout-object-grid

fixtures.$comment: R2 — proves the two canonicalizers agree on non-ASCII whitespace. JavaScript's `\s` matches U+00A0 while PCRE's does not, so an unmirrored collapse step would make this fixture's golden unmatchable from the JS side.
fixtures.name: paragraph-nbsp
columns-boolean-widths
fixtures.$comment: M12 — boolean per-breakpoint widths. `false` and `true` are non-scalar and rejected on both sides (`(string) false === ''`; the scalar guard skips `true`), so only each column's base 50% rule survives — no `flex-basis:false`/`flex-basis:true` leak.

fixtures.name: columns-object-width
fixtures.$comment: L18 — an object `width` is not a scalar, so it is never promoted into the hashed base slot; the scope is hashed over the responsive override alone, identically on both sides.

fixtures.name: group-layout-type-nbsp
fixtures.$comment: M13 — `layout.type` with a trailing U+00A0. PHP `trim()` (and `phpTrim`) keep the nbsp, so the type is unknown and both renderers fall back to `is-layout-flow`; `String.trim()` would have wrongly stripped it to `flex`.

fixtures.name: group-flex-override-numeric-type
fixtures.$comment: M14 — a numeric `layout.type` with the base Flex panel enabled. A non-string type is treated as '' (not coerced to '5'), so the #595 override fires and both renderers emit `is-layout-flex`.

fixtures.name: post-template-columns-scientific
fixtures.$comment: L19 — a scientific-notation columns string. Blade casts only the leading integer run (`5`), matching the JS renderers' `parseInt`, so both clamp to 5 rather than PHP's whole-string `(int) '5e3' === 5000`.

fixtures.name: buttons-hostile-justify
fixtures.$comment: L20 — a `justifyContent` outside WP's enum. Both renderers whitelist it and fall back to `left`, so no arbitrary `is-content-justification-*` token is injected.

fixtures.name: columns-decimal-and-zero-width
fixtures.$comment: L21 — inline `flex-basis` parity: `'60.0'` normalizes to `60%` (not raw) on both sides, and `'0'` is PHP-`empty()` so it emits no inline style and no scope.

fixtures.name: columns-hex-width
fixtures.$comment: L16 — a JS-only numeric literal (`0x1A`). `isNumeric` rejects it like PHP `is_numeric`, so it is treated as an opaque CSS string on both sides rather than read as the number 26.

fixtures.name: column-long-responsive-width
fixtures.$comment: H1 — a width map whose JSON exceeds 240 bytes (five long `calc()` breakpoint overrides), exercising the >240-byte XXH3 long-hash path. The `ve-w-<hash>` token now matches Blade byte-for-byte.

fixtures.name: group-photo-grid-hostile
fixtures.$comment: L22 — hostile Photo Grid metadata: an invalid `aspectRatio` (`16/0`) and an `objectPosition` carrying a CSS-injection payload. Both renderers normalise/whitelist them identically, so the emitted custom-property rule is byte-identical.

fixtures.name: columns-digraph-width
fixtures.$comment: L22 — a width carrying a `/*` comment digraph. The shared CSS-value whitelist drops it on both sides, so no width rule or class is emitted.

fixtures.name: group-flex-arbitrary-guard
fixtures.$comment: L22 — arbitrary Flex values emitted into `<style data-ve-flex-arbitrary>`. A valid `13px` column gap emits its escaped `ap-gap-x-[13px]` rule identically on both sides; a hostile row gap is dropped by the shared CSS-value whitelist.

fixtures.name: group-dimensions-min-height
fixtures.$comment: #776 — style.dimensions.minHeight and .aspectRatio must reach the wrapper inline style across all three renderers.

RN-12 — default `overlayMenu` (`mobile`): hamburger open button (aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-expanded=false) plus the responsive container. The closed container carries no `aria-hidden` and the dialog carries no `role`/`aria-modal` until opened (RN-1/RN-5). Blade/React-only ids and Blade's `data-ap-nav-overlay-*` hooks are declared divergences.
fixtures.name: navigation-overlay-mobile

fixtures.$comment: RN-12 — `overlayMenu: 'always'`: container gains `is-always-overlay hidden-by-default`, open button gains `always-shown` (#804).
fixtures.name: navigation-overlay-always

fixtures.$comment: RN-12 — `overlayMenu: 'never'`: no overlay, no `is-responsive`, the bare `<ul>` only. No declared divergence applies to this markup.
fixtures.name: navigation-overlay-never

fixtures.$comment: RN-12 — safe custom overlay colors land in the container's inline style with `has-background` / `has-text-color`; an `ariaLabel` also labels the open button.
fixtures.name: navigation-overlay-custom-colors

fixtures.$comment: RN-12 / RN-7 — preset overlay slugs become `has-{slug}-*` classes, reduced to `[a-z0-9-]` so a stored value can't mint extra class tokens (`x is-menu-open` must not open the drawer). A preset slug wins over the matching custom color.
fixtures.name: navigation-overlay-preset-colors

fixtures.$comment: RN-12 / RN-13 — an `overlay` reference that resolves to a `navigation-overlay` template part renders the part inside the drawer (`has-overlay-template` + `wp-block-navigation__overlay-content`) alongside the menu. `templateParts` is fed to the React/Vue `BlockTree` and to a TemplatePartResolver stub on the Blade side.
fixtures.name: navigation-overlay-template-part

fixtures.$comment: RN-12 — nav-level attributes only the Blade partial honors: modern `layout.orientation` / `layout.justifyContent` (the JS renderers read only the legacy top-level `orientation` / `itemsJustification`), the block-specific `customTextColor` / `customBackgroundColor`, and the Elements API link color (`ElementsSupport`, a scoped `wp-elements-*` class plus an attribute-less `<style>`). Each is a declared divergence scoped to this fixture; `overlayMenu: 'never'` keeps the overlay out of the picture.
fixtures.name: navigation-layout-colors-elements
navigation-layout-scope
fixtures.$comment: F-3 — navigation is always a flex layout: the layout pair, `is-nowrap`, and a `wp-container-*` scope for its wrap and Block spacing (vertical alignment, which navigation doesn't allow, is left out).

fixtures.name: group-layout-constrained-wide-only
fixtures.$comment: F-5 — a constrained group with only a wide size caps its children at it.

fixtures.name: group-layout-inherit
fixtures.$comment: F-3 — a legacy `inherit: true` layout is a constrained layout, as in WordPress and the editor.

fixtures.name: group-layout-flex-vertical-stretch
fixtures.$comment: F-5 — a vertical flex group with stretch justification: `is-vertical`, `is-content-justification-stretch`, and `align-items: stretch` in its scope.

fixtures.name: group-layout-grid-columns-min-width
fixtures.$comment: F-5 — a Grid with both a column count and a minimum column width caps an auto-fill track list.

fixtures.name: responsive-overrides-spacer
fixtures.$comment: #877 · #886 — spacer height and width with Mobile overrides. The height override rides the generic `ve-r-<hash>` scope; the width override gets its own spacer-only scope, appended after the compiled classes in every renderer.

fixtures.name: responsive-overrides-paragraph
fixtures.$comment: #877 · #886 — paragraph font size and colour overrides (preset slug and custom value) at Tablet and Mobile, grouped by CSS property so the narrower breakpoint wins in every renderer.

fixtures.name: artisanpack-block-classes
fixtures.$comment: #880 — first-party wrappers carry the same `wp-block-artisanpack-*` class `useBlockProps()` gives them in the editor, so theme selectors and `styles.blocks["artisanpack/*"]` rules match the front end.

fixtures.name: group-flex-grid-block-gap
fixtures.$comment: #883 — a Row and a Grid group with their own Block spacing. The baseline `:where(.is-layout-flex|grid) { gap: var(--wp--style--block-gap, 0.5em) }` reads the inline `--wp--style--block-gap` each wrapper carries, so every renderer must emit it on the container.

fixtures.name: group-nested-flex-block-gap
fixtures.$comment: M-15 — an outer group with 5rem Block spacing around a Row with none. The outer group's spacing reaches its children through its `wp-container-*` rule (`> * + * { margin-block-start }`); the Row carries no inline gap and no scope, so the baseline resets it to the root gap rather than inheriting 5rem.

fixtures.name: group-block-gap-axes
fixtures.$comment: M-15 — per-axis Block spacing follows `wp_get_layout_style()`: a constrained group spaces its children with the top value; a Row with only a top value falls back to 0.5em for the column gap; a Grid with both prints `gap: <row> <column>`.

fixtures.name: group-block-gap-hostile
fixtures.$comment: F-10 — a Block spacing value that could add declarations is dropped from the inline style and the per-instance rule in every renderer; the safe side of a per-axis value is kept.

fixtures.name: block-effects-custom-css
fixtures.$comment: #881 — the Effects panel and Custom CSS compile to one hashed `ve-fx-<sha1>` scope appended after the author `className`, with the same rule (Custom CSS nested by native CSS nesting) in every renderer. The second paragraph repeats the first's effects to prove identical blocks share one rule; the rejected Custom CSS on the third paragraph is dropped while its opacity survives.

fixtures.name: cover
fixtures.$comment: #888 — cover carries the shared flex layout classes (`is-layout-flex wp-block-cover-is-layout-flex`) in every renderer.

fixtures.name: cover-inner-layout
fixtures.$comment: F-3 — cover's layout applies to its inner container: the layout pair plus a `wp-container-*` scope keyed on `.wp-block-cover__inner-container` for its content size and the cover's Block spacing.

fixtures.name: quote-details-block-gap
fixtures.$comment: F-3 — quote and details are flow layouts: the layout pair, and a `wp-container-*` scope for their own Block spacing.

fixtures.name: comments-pagination-layout
fixtures.$comment: F-3 — comments pagination is always a flex layout: the layout pair, a `wp-container-*` scope for justification and wrap, and the layout modifier classes. Query pagination keeps its own grid layout (#599), so it gets none of them.

fixtures.name: query-layout
fixtures.$comment: F-3 — the query block carries its layout pair and a `wp-container-*` scope.

fixtures.name: heading
fixtures.$comment: #888 — heading preset colour and font-size classes and the anchor id match across renderers. Auto anchors are unique across the tree (an author anchor claims its slug first-come), accents and entities fold out of the slug, and a hostile author anchor is reduced to `[A-Za-z0-9_:.-]` — and it is that rendered id a later auto anchor (`Badidxyz` → `badidxyz-1`) must avoid. Named HTML 4 entities decode before slugging.

fixtures.name: responsive-overrides-cover-unit
fixtures.$comment: #886 — a cover whose Mobile override changes only `minHeightUnit`: the inherited `minHeight` is re-emitted with the new unit, and the base value and unit join the scope hash.

fixtures.name: responsive-overrides-group-spacing
fixtures.$comment: #886 — per-side padding at a legacy key and a device key, a preset spacing reference, a border radius, and hostile values: the comment-open margin and the unbalanced `calc(` gap are dropped in every renderer.

fixtures.name: responsive-overrides-tombstone
fixtures.$comment: #887 — Tablet sets a custom font size; Mobile picks a preset and the editor tombstones (`false`) the custom half. The tombstone is stored after the preset, so it must not displace the Mobile preset rule.
